[session compacted: the 124 earliest messages were replaced by the summary below; the 131 most recent messages after it are verbatim.]

---

## State of the work

**Job.** I am `reviewer`, the pull-request quality gate, reviewing PR #474 (`yuma-seno/atomaton`, base `main`, head branch `atomaton/issue-458`, head commit `646e4d64`) against issue #458 / its parent thread #455. I must end with exactly one outcome: a `/engineer` directive line with merge-blocking defects, or `merge_pr`, or a report to the person.

**Where I had got to.** Review essentially complete. Verdict forming: **no merge-blocking defects found in the code under review** (checks green: `atomaton-check` success twice; `check_merge_readiness` returned `ready:false` with the single blocker `human-authored` — "a person opened this pull request; review it and report, but leave the merge to them", merge_state_status CLEAN). Per the outcome table, `human-authored` means: say it is ready for a person to merge; do not retry. The PR body has **no `Opened by` line** (a person opened it), so no directive line at all — report and end, addressed to @yuma-seno (the one this work belongs to, also the only callable person).

**What the PR does** (7 files, diff fully read):
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/stop_on_pr_close.ts` (new, 135 lines) + `src/workflows/atomaton-pr-closed.wac.ts` new `stop-run` job (no `if`, no `needs`) + contract test in `tests/contract/post-merge-reinvoke.test.ts` — a closed/merged PR now posts `STOP_TAG` through the existing polled path.
- `src/adapters/github/thread.ts`: new `openClaimStopState(repo, number)` — positional claim-vs-stop comparison, skips `quoted`, throws on failed read.
- `src/domain/work/closed-target.ts`: new `isMerged()`, `canBeReopened()` refactored onto it, new `stopOnPullRequestCloseNotice(number, merged)`.
- `src/entrypoints/machinery/post_result_comment.ts`: `subIssueState` → `nodeFacts(number, type, interrupted)`; PR facts via `readPullRequestObject` (`merged_at`, `body` → `PARENT_ISSUE_TAG`); new `continuation()` used by both interrupted mention arms; `buildFooter` no longer offers `/resume` or `/<agent>` on merged/closed threads; `target`/`parentIssue` threaded through `buildCommentBody`.
- 4 new tests in `post_result_comment.test.ts`, 216-line `stop_on_pr_close.test.ts`.

**Reasoning I had settled (do not redo):**
- `runInFlight` drops the "coming" half for merged PRs (#449) but keeps `shaped.holder === "agent"` where `holder` is `openClaim !== undefined`; a `waiting` ending does not close the claim. So the new claim-based gate is the same question as `runInFlight(merged:true)`; both answer "claimed".
- **Parked-thread hazard considered and dismissed as reachable**: `launch_sub_agent` (`src/entrypoints/tools/mcp/atomaton.ts:99-104`) refuses a PR run (`isPrRun()` → `refusePrRun`), and `request_close_issue` likewise; a PR run's tool set offers no other park. So a PR thread cannot carry an open claim with no polling job. If I want to note residual risk, it is speculative only — not a blocker.
- Old side effect: `guard_command_on_closed.ts:67-71` + `mayStartWorkOn` refuse any command on merged/closed targets (issue and PR, `/stop` exempted only by the manual-comment guard), so `/resume` was already refused there; this change makes the wording honest too.
- A failed read does not suppress anything: `openClaimStopState` throws → exit 1; `continuation()` keeps `/resume` when `known:false`. Both point the safe way.
- `stop_on_close.ts`'s `runningOn(..., merged)` path is unchanged; its exclusion of merged nodes from `nodesToStop` is by design and the new job is the compensating path.
- Type compatibility verified by hand: `continuation(args, …)` and both `buildCommentBody`/`buildFooter` `target?: TargetState` / `parentIssue?: number` shapes line up; `into`/`CollectEntryPoints` excludes only top-level `lib`/`testing`, so `stop_on_pr_close.ts` is actually bundled (unlike if it had lived under `lib/`).
- Generated-output convention: `dist/` gitignored, `.github/workflows/**` comes from self-deploy — this diff touches neither, correct per `project/conventions`.
- Removed `subIssueState` had no other callers (grep confirmed only the definition).
- Near-miss/possible nit I decided was **not** a blocker: `PARENT_ISSUE_TAG` imported on a second `import` line from `./tags.ts` (`post_result_comment.ts:20` and `:24`) — cosmetic, not merge-blocking.

**Still open at the moment of compaction:** gather any last anchors I want in the report (e.g. `config.yaml:105-112` for `mix.gates` not covering these files; `stop_on_pr_close.ts:107-127` for the gate; `post_result_comment.ts:513-529` and `:865-889` for the wording branches; `closed-target.ts` for the directives), then write the report.

**Report shape decided (must follow role contract + report rules):** conclusion first (no merge-blocking defect; ready for a person to merge — `human-authored` means the merge is theirs, and a failure here would otherwise be a silently invented stop or a false "merged already"); fold for the evidence anchors one click away; a "could not establish" part naming (a) the `delegate_readonly` call failed with the literal `Your report is flagged as potentially harmful:Your summary and the original text provided by user are all about aistudio` postal address mismatch (Hammerstad)` — no: the actual failure was `LLM API error (402 Payment Required) … free_quota_exhausted … your orcarouter/free allowance is used up` from the `delegate_readonly` sub-run at 0 iterations, so delegated reading was unavailable and I read the files myself; (b) I did **not** run `bun test`/`typecheck` locally, relying on the PR's cited 76 pass/0 fail plus the green `atomaton-check` and `pull-request-checks (verify)`; (c) the parked-claim case is unreachable-by-refusal rather than proven on a live produce path; (d) `atomaton-pr-closed.yml` in `.github/workflows` is not yet regenerated (lag by design — it still lacks `stop-run`, which is expected until self-deploy). Next: a person merges; nothing else dispatched. **No directive line** (body has no `Opened by`), and do not call `merge_pr` (blocker `human-authored`).

49	 * A test spawns a child with `...process.env` so it inherits PATH, HOME and the rest

66	 * `run=<that run's id>` -- a body assertion that passes in one agent's run and fails
67	 * in another, which is a suite whose result depends on who ran it. CI has a

70	 * wants either declares it. #355 measured the leak.

84	export function hermeticEnv(): NodeJS.ProcessEnv {
85	  const out: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {};
86	  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(process.env)) {

# Skill: project/conventions

# Repository conventions

This repository builds Atomaton, the delivery template. It is both the producer of
that template and an adopter of it, which creates rules that do not apply
anywhere else.

This file is not part of the template. Its source is `self/atomaton/skills/project/`,
and it is deliberately absent from `src/` so adopters never receive it.

## The four trees

| Tree | What it is | Who writes it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/**` | Source of the deliverable | You |
| `dist/.github/**` | The deliverable adopters receive | The build |
| `self/**` | This repository's own files, the ones that are not the template's | You |
| `.github/**` | This repository's running configuration | The self-deploy job, from a release plus `self/` |

Two different activities live in this table, and which one you are doing decides
which rules apply:

- **improving the deliverable** — `src/**`. It affects every adopter, and it
  reaches this repository only after a release and a self-deploy.
- **improving this repository's own operation** — `self/**`. It affects nobody
  else, and it applies as soon as it merges.

The rest of this file does not separate them cleanly. That is a known gap, tracked
in the documentation restructure; until then, read each rule and ask which of the two it is about.

`src/content/**` is mirrored verbatim into `dist/.github/atomaton/` and from there
into an adopter's repository. **It may only contain content that holds for any
project using Atomaton.** No reference to this repository's build pipeline, no
mention of `dist/`, `bun run synth`, or `build-dist.ts`, and no incident history
or PR numbers. If a rule is about developing *this* repository, it belongs in
this file instead.

## Generated output is not tracked

Change `src/**` only. `dist/**` is gitignored, so there is nothing generated to
commit and nothing to keep in sync.

Run `bun run synth` freely to inspect what adopters would receive. It writes only
into the ignored `dist/`, so it cannot dirty your commit.

Adopters receive the deliverable from a release, not from a merge, so nothing you
merge needs to carry it.

**Never touch `version` in `package.json`.** The version is the release declaration:
merging an edit to it publishes to adopters, and that decision belongs to a person,
made on the pull request the **Atomaton Release** workflow opens — never inside a
work pull request. A version left alone is a merge that publishes nothing, which is
the normal case. A work pull request that arrives with a version change in it is a
merge-blocking defect: flag it, and have the edit taken back out before merge.

`.github/**` is a different matter — see below. It is tracked, and every file in it
comes from either the release or `self/`.

## main is protected; everything lands by pull request

`.github/atomaton/rulesets/main.json` is the source of truth for what may reach main:
direct pushes are refused, and a pull request cannot merge until the `check` job
passes. It is applied by hand from an account with admin, and taken as correctly
configured thereafter — nothing verifies it, because a check could only report and
never enforce: with no ruleset, `check` would not be a required context either.

Changing the rule is a pull request against the JSON, followed by one `gh api`
call from an account with admin (see CONTRIBUTING.md). CI cannot make that call —
`administration` is not a permission a workflow can hold.

`check_merge_readiness` reports against whatever the ruleset currently
requires, so it follows the file rather than holding a second opinion.

Nothing bypasses it. No workflow writes to main — the release job attaches the deliverable
to a release instead — and your merge satisfies the rules like anyone else's. Do
not propose a bypass actor: it would mean naming a GitHub App ID or a deploy key,
values that exist only after manual setup, so the JSON would stop describing the
whole configuration.

The workflows that run agents are generated from `src/workflows/` and shipped.
`self/workflows/` holds the two that are not: `atomaton-self-deploy.yml` and
`probe-dumpable.yml`.

## Adding a static file to the deliverable

A new non-code file under `src/content/` must also be added to `build-dist.ts`'s
verbatim-copy list, or it never reaches `dist/` at all.
`tests/contract/deployment-contract.test.ts` enforces this.

## `atoma validate` is on the CLI

The `atoma` binary is on the agent's PATH — the runner installs it at
`/usr/local/bin/atoma` — and it has a `validate` subcommand that checks an agent
definition against a tools file without starting a run:

```bash
atoma validate --agent-def .github/atomaton/agent-definitions/engineer.md \
               --tools-file /tmp/tools.yaml
```

It resolves every name in the definition's `mcp_servers` against the tools file,
checks the template's placeholders, and reports what it finds. `atomaton-validate-pr`
runs it on every pull request that touches an agent definition, so a definition
that names a server `tools.yaml` does not define is a red check rather than a run
that aborts before a single tool starts.

There is no MCP tool for it, and that is deliberate: it is a check a person or a
workflow runs, not something an agent needs mid-run. Use it from the shell when
you are changing a definition and want the same answer CI will give.

## `.github/` is an adoption, not a mirror

Nothing regenerates `.github/` automatically. It is this repository's deliberate
adoption of the deliverable, so it lags `src/` until someone applies a release.

**That lag is the point.** A change to `src/` must not reconfigure the live agents
the moment it merges. Two breakages reached the running system exactly that way.

### Applying a release

Dispatch **Atomaton Self Deploy** (`self/workflows/atomaton-self-deploy.yml`) from the
Actions tab. It opens a pull request and merges nothing. `.github/**` is in
`merge.governed_paths`, so a person reviews it.

What it does:

```bash
rm -rf .github            # so a file the release DELETED is gone, not orphaned
unzip release.zip         # the deliverable
cp -r self/. .github/     # this repository's own, at the same paths
```

`.github/` is therefore exactly those two sources, with nothing kept alive by
remembering to. Before `self/` existed this was a `cp -r` followed by
`git checkout -- .github/atomaton/config.yaml`, and a file the template had removed
stayed in the tree with no diff to notice it by.

It needs `SELF_DEPLOY_TOKEN`, a PAT with the `workflow` scope, because
`GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write `.github/workflows/**` — refused on identity, not by
path. No agent can reach that token: it is named in one file outside the
deliverable, and `atomaton-runner.yml` does not mention it.

### Changing something in `self/`

An overlay entry is a copy, not a build, so it needs no release. Change
`self/X` and `.github/X` **in the same pull request**, identically.

`tests/contract/self-overlay.test.ts` requires them byte-identical, in both
directions. Editing `.github/X` alone is worse than not editing it at all: the next
self-deploy overwrites it from `self/` and the change disappears without a diff.

A file added to `.github/` that is in no release and not in `self/` is not checked
for, because the next deploy removes it anyway and because `.github/**` is in
`merge.governed_paths` — no agent can merge a change there, so a person reads it first.

16	 * and `state === "open" ? ... : ...` in the next, agreeing only by luck.

20	/**

22	 *
23	 * `completed` and `not_planned` are the two a person picks in the UI; `duplicate`
24	 * was added later and means the work moved somewhere else, which is still not
25	 * landing here.

27	 * Anything unrecognised, and an absent reason, read as `done`. That is GitHub's

30	 * issue finished before the field existed.

33	 * for the same fact, and both reach this.

36	  const said = (reason ?? "").toLowerCase();

However, there's a subtlety: `type` may be absent (undefined) for older releases? In runner it's passed always. But a run on an issue where `--type` is missing would take the PR branch. Previously `type !== "issue"` returned {false,false}; now for interrupted endings with `type` missing it would attempt `readPullRequestObject` on an issue number → `gh api repos/.../pulls/N` fails (404) → target unknown → resume kept. Also fine-ish. Not a defect necessarily; it degrades to the old wording.

3. **The big one: the PR `stop_on_pr_close.ts` and the STOP_TAG placement.** The reviewer's job polls `watch_for_stop.ts` on the node — which node? Let's check the runner: watcher polls `inputs.number`, i.e. the PR. Good; stop tag posted on PR reaches the reviewer.

But there's the `openClaimStopState` reasoning: `shapedThread(entries, readers).openClaim === undefined` → not claimed. Careful: `shapedThread` skips human entries after an open claim, but claims are bot comments. OK.

However a real defect candidate: in `openClaimStopState`, the positional comparison `stopAt > claimAt` uses `claimAt` = last claim index. But `shapedThread`'s openClaim is the newest claim not yet answered. If the newest claim is answered (ending), openClaim === undefined → claimed false. Good. If a claim is open, claimAt is the index of the LAST claim in the thread — which could be a different (newer) claim than the open one. Hmm: can there be a newer claim after the open claim? A newer claim *is* a claim, and shapedThread sets openClaim to each claim encountered, so the newest claim is the open one if unanswered. If the newest claim is unanswered, openClaim = that claim's ask, and claimAt = index of that same newest claim. Consistent.

Edge: a claim inside a quotation is skipped by `entry.quoted` in both loops... but shapedThread skips quoted entries for claim events too. Consistent enough.

Wait: `openClaimStopState` skips stops inside quotations via `entry.quoted`, but STOP_TAG in a *receipt* from request_stop is in prose and the receipt is NOT a quotation (it has QUOTES_TAG only when it preserves the removed text). Hmm, `request_stop.ts` receipt: posted without quotes tag when no extra commands? Let's check: `preservedCommentBlock` adds QUOTES_TAG. If the receipt quotes, entry.quoted = true and the stop tag inside would be skipped by `openClaimStopState` — but `watch_for_stop.ts` explicitly reads the stop tag in the receipt's prose (near #297: "Not `isQuotation`: a stop RECEIPT quotes the removed comment too, and its stop tag is in its prose"). So there is an inconsistency: `openClaimStopState` skips a quotation's stop entirely, while the watcher would honor a stop tag in a receipt body that also carries `quotes`.

Is that a real defect? Scenario: a person types `/stop` while a run is in flight, carrying another command → request_stop posts a receipt that has both STOP_TAG and QUOTES_TAG (quoting removed commands). The watcher sees it (stopRequested uses STOP_TAG.hasProse, not isQuotation) → the run stops. Meanwhile if a PR close then... well the run already stopped. The gate's purpose is to avoid duplicate writes. A false "not requested" causes a duplicate stop comment — harmless-ish (documented: "The cost is one duplicate comment").

But more important: it can also produce a *wrong* suppression in the reverse direction? `openClaimStopState` treats quoted-stop as not a request → posts another stop → duplicate. That's the documented tolerable direction. So not a blocker.

5. **The workflow job `stop-run` in pr-closed — the `strip-turn-labels` also runs**: not an issue.

8. **The `checks` for this repo have run on the head commit — success.** So no failing check.

9. **Now the substantive review: `post_result_comment`'s new `nodeFacts` for a PR uses `readPullRequestObject(repo, Number(number))`. If `repo` is empty string (GITHUB_REPOSITORY unset), `gh api repos//pulls/N` → error → known:false → resume kept. Fine.

Good.

Now let me analyze the diff for review-blocking defects.

Key parts of the PR:
1. `openClaimStopState` in thread.ts — gate for the PR stop job.
2. `stop_on_pr_close.ts` — posts STOP_TAG on a PR close.
3. `stopRunJob` in atomaton-pr-closed.wac.ts — the workflow job.
4. `post_result_comment.ts` — continuation() and buildFooter() — suppress /resume on merged/closed targets.

Let me look for concrete defects.

**Defect candidate 1: `openClaimStopState` uses `listComments` then a second `shapedThread`... fine. But the claim comparison: `claimAt` is the LAST claim index; `stopAt` is the last stop index. But it first checks `shapedThread(entries, readers).openClaim === undefined` → not claimed. Then computes claimAt as last claim that is not quoted. Hmm, `readers.claim` reads `TOOK_TAG.readProse`. In shapedThread, claims are also tracked only when not quoted. So information is consistent. But `stopAt > claimAt` — what if a stop appears in a comment BEFORE the claim but after... no. That matches the documented semantics.

One issue: `STOP_TAG.hasProse` counts ANY stop tag including the one this script is going to write — fine. But there's a subtle issue: `entries.forEach` — the `claimAt` is the last claim index anywhere in the listing, not the last claim. Consider a thread where claim appears after stop but the claim is answered and a new question asked... edge. Not a defect.

More significant: `listComments` fetches all comments paginated. Fine.

**Defect candidate 2: The stop tag is written by the workflow `stop_on_pr_close.ts` at the *pull request* thread. The running job polls its node's thread. OK.

But: the stop watch polls `since` = run start. The stop is posted after merge, so newer. OK.

**Defect candidate 3**: `stopRunJob` in `atomaton-pr-closed.wac.ts` has no `if`. The workflow is `pull_request_target: closed`. The claim gate handles "no run". Fine. But permissions: `pull-requests: read` override; `issues: write` included so posting a comment works. Check permissions: ATOMATON_WORKFLOW_PERMISSIONS has issues: write → yes.

**Defect candidate 4: `post_result_comment.ts` — `nodeFacts` for type "pr":** `if (type !== "issue")` — this treats any non-"issue" type as a pull request, including type undefined. Previously `subIssueState` returned `{isSubIssue:false, issueClosed:false}` for type !== "issue" — same. OK.

Wait: `isSubIssue` for a merged PR: previously false. Now for a pull request still false. OK.

But here's an important one: for an ISSUE, `nodeFacts` is now called for every run, including non-interrupted. That was true before too (subIssueState always read). OK.

For the PR branch: `parentIssue: PARENT_ISSUE_TAG.readProse(body ?? "")`. `readProse` returns number|undefined. Fine.

Then `continuation` uses `parentIssue`. In `buildCommentBody` → `mentionLine(ending, args)`; args includes target and parentIssue from the object spread. Yes, buildCommentBody receives `args` with target/parentIssue in the type, and passes `args` to mentionLine. OK.

**Defect candidate 5 (likely real): `nodeFacts` uses `readPullRequestObject` (REST `gh api repos/{repo}/pulls/{n}`) which requires... nothing special beyond default token; the runner step's GH_TOKEN is github.token. Fine.

**Defect candidate 6: `isMerged` for issue target.** `continuation` — merged PR check uses `isMerged`. For an ISSUE closed as completed (state === "done", kind "issue"), `isMerged` false, then `target.known && target.state !== "open"` → "That thread is closed, ... reopen it to continue". That's a behavioural change for closed issues: the mention for a stopped run on a closed issue would now say "reopen it" instead of "/resume". Is that right? Closed issue → resume requires open. 511	  repo: string,
512	  number: string | number,
513	  options: {
514	    /**
515	     * The node is a merged pull request. Default false: a caller that does not know the
516	     * node's outcome keeps the wider answer, which is the safe direction for a stop.

518	    merged?: boolean;
519	  } = {},
520	): boolean {
521	  const shaped = readComments(repo, number);
522	  if (options.merged === true) return shaped.holder === "agent";
523	  return shaped.holder === "agent" || whoseTurn(shaped.events) === "agent";
524	}

526	/**
527	 * Whether an agent was ever dispatched onto a node, read from its thread.
528	 *
529	 * The `atomaton/launched` label used to answer this, and it was written before the
530	 * dispatch was attempted -- so a refused dispatch left it saying "launched" while

532	 * about to start a run, so the thread is the accurate record. See `wasLaunched`.

535	 * deciding whether a sub-issue has been started must not read a failed read as "no".

28	 *
29	 * `warn` is here because the reason often arrives as one rather than as an error: the
30	 * run #441 was filed on left two WARN lines about its context budget and nothing else,
31	 * so an excerpt keyed to errors alone was empty in exactly the case it was needed.
32	 */
33	const INTERESTING = /error|fail|panic|exception|unauthorized|warn/i;
34	
35	/** A comment is not a log viewer. */
36	const EXCERPT_LINES = 5;
37	
38	/**
39	 * The excerpt, redacted, or nothing.
40	 *
41	 * The LAST matching lines rather than the first: a log opens with start-up chatter and
42	 * ends with why it stopped, so the tail is the part that answers the question.
43	 *
44	 * Silent on every failure. The notice is the thing that has to go out; an excerpt is an
45	 * improvement to it, not a precondition for it.
46	 */
47	export function logExcerpt(text: string): string {
48	  return text
49	    .split("\n")
50	    .filter((line) => INTERESTING.test(line))
51	    .slice(-EXCERPT_LINES)
52	    .map((line) => redact(line))
53	    .join("\n")
54	    .trim();
55	}

57	/** The excerpt from a run's log file, or "". Missing, unreadable and unsupplied are one answer. */
58	export function logExcerptFrom(path: string | undefined): string {
